pr.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

raw_findings.body: Every signup attempt with a blocked email inflates match_count by 2 instead of 1 (and any other code calling `valid?` further inflates it), so the blocked-email statistics the feature is meant to track are systematically wrong; validation also performs unexpected DB writes even inside read-only `valid?` checks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: match_count and last_match_at are updated on every validation pass, producing double-counted and spurious statistics plus DB writes on non-persisting valid? calls.
raw_findings.impact: Every signup attempt with a blocked email inflates match_count by 2 instead of 1 (and any other code calling `valid?` further inflates it), so the blocked-email statistics the feature is meant to track are systematically wrong; validation also performs unexpected DB writes even inside read-only `valid?` checks.
raw_findings.root_cause: State-mutating statistics update embedded inside an ActiveModel validator that Rails runs multiple times per request.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Split the side effect out of validation: have should_block? only read, and record the match (increment/update timestamp) once at a single point in the create flow, or guard the stats update so it runs at most once per request.
raw_findings.title: BlockedEmail.should_block? mutates DB during validation and double-increments match_count per signup attempt
raw_findings.trigger: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` (line 168, before DiscourseHub registration) and then `user.save` (line 172); each run of validations invokes EmailValidator#validate_each, which calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and writes last_match_at.

raw_findings.body: Lost updates: concurrent increments overwrite each other, so match_count undercounts actual block events.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Race window between read and save causes concurrent block events to be counted as one.
raw_findings.impact: Lost updates: concurrent increments overwrite each other, so match_count undercounts actual block events.
raw_findings.root_cause: In-memory increment followed by save instead of an atomic database-level counter update.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an atomic SQL update, e.g. BlockedEmail.where(email: email).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now]), instead of load-increment-save.
raw_findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count in should_block?
raw_findings.trigger: Two or more concurrent signup attempts using the same blocked email address hit should_block? at the same time; each loads the row, increments its in-memory copy, and saves.

raw_findings.body: Emails rejected in one instance leak into every other instance's validation, causing emails to be flagged as invalid in contexts where they were never rejected; state also can never be reset by creating a fresh controller.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cross-instance state bleed of rejected emails leading to false-positive validation failures.
raw_findings.impact: Emails rejected in one instance leak into every other instance's validation, causing emails to be flagged as invalid in contexts where they were never rejected; state also can never be reset by creating a fresh controller.
raw_findings.root_cause: Mutable array literal placed in the Ember class definition hash, which Ember shares across all instances rather than cloning per instance.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the array per instance, e.g. set `rejectedEmails: null` in the class body and assign `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A())` in an `init` hook.
raw_findings.title: rejectedEmails Em.A defined on class prototype creates shared mutable state across controller instances
raw_findings.trigger: Any situation where more than one CreateAccountController instance is created (e.g. controller re-instantiation in tests or future non-singleton use); all instances share the single Em.A array created at class-definition time because object-valued properties on an Ember class extend hash are shared, not per-instance.

raw_findings.body: The user sees "Please enter a valid email address." (client key user.email.invalid) for an address that is perfectly valid in format but blocked/rejected by the server, giving incorrect guidance; the server-side 'blocked: "is not allowed."' wording is never surfaced.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Misleading validation feedback that tells users their correctly formatted email is malformed.
raw_findings.impact: The user sees "Please enter a valid email address." (client key user.email.invalid) for an address that is perfectly valid in format but blocked/rejected by the server, giving incorrect guidance; the server-side 'blocked: "is not allowed."' wording is never surfaced.
raw_findings.root_cause: Reuse of the format-validation message for a semantically different server-rejection condition.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a distinct client locale key (e.g. user.email.rejected or user.email.blocked in client.en.yml) and use it for the rejectedEmails branch instead of reusing user.email.invalid.
raw_findings.title: Server-rejected (blocked) emails shown with misleading 'invalid email' client message
raw_findings.trigger: A user submits a syntactically valid but blocked email; the server returns an email error, the address is pushed to rejectedEmails, and emailValidation re-renders the reason for that address.

raw_findings.body: Violates POSIX text-file convention followed by the rest of the repository; produces noisy diffs when the file is next edited and can trip lint/CI newline checks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Convention violation causing spurious diff noise and potential lint failures.
raw_findings.impact: Violates POSIX text-file convention followed by the rest of the repository; produces noisy diffs when the file is next edited and can trip lint/CI newline checks.
raw_findings.root_cause: New file created without a terminating newline character.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a trailing newline at the end of lib/validators/email_validator.rb.
raw_findings.title: lib/validators/email_validator.rb missing trailing newline
raw_findings.trigger: The new file is committed without a final newline, as flagged by the patch's '\ No newline at end of file' marker.
